lyrics:
[Intro: arpeggiated electric guitar in six, soft organ]

[Verse 1: raw soulful female voice, quiet]
You called me by your sister's name
You asked me when the war would end
You told the nurse I was a kind old lady
Who comes on Thursdays, like a friend

[Pre-Chorus: backing voices "ooh", drums enter]
And I said, "That's right, baby. That's me."

[Chorus: full doo-wop band, voice breaking open]
But you still know my hand
Oh, you reach, and there I am
Fifty years, you don't know who I am
But you still know my hand
Call me whoever you want to, man
You still know my hand

[Verse 2: voice rougher, piano triplets]
They tell me I should rest, go home
They say you won't know if I do
But I was there when you were handsome
I was there when you were cruel, when you were kind, when you were you

[Pre-Chorus: backing voices "ooh"]
So I'll be the lady. That's fine by me.

[Chorus: full doo-wop band, voice breaking open]
'Cause you still know my hand
Oh, you reach, and there I am
Fifty years, you don't know who I am
But you still know my hand
Call me whoever you want to, man
You still know my hand

[Bridge: band drops low, voice nearly a scream]
I'm tired! Lord, I'm tired!
And I'd do it all again

[Final Chorus: biggest, backing voices answering]
You still know my hand (you still know)
Oh, you reach, and there I am
Fifty years, you don't know who I am
But you still know my hand
Call me whoever you want to, man
You still know my hand

[Outro: guitar arpeggio, humming, "It's Thursday, baby."]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 57 BPM, 6/8, G major. A slow, rocking 1950s doo-wop sway.

VOICE: Female, an older, lived-in soul voice. She croons the verses softly, breaks into a rasp in the choruses and almost screams the bridge. Three backing singers sing 'ooh' and answer her in the last chorus. She speaks the last line tenderly.

INSTRUMENTS: A clean electric guitar playing slow arpeggios, piano triplets, a Hammond organ, an upright-style bass, a drum kit with brushes and a heavy backbeat, backing vocal group, a string section in the final chorus.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, guitar and organ. 0:16 Verse 1. 0:50 Pre-chorus. 1:00 Chorus 1. 1:36 Verse 2. 2:10 Pre-chorus. 2:18 Chorus 2. 2:54 Bridge. 3:08 Final chorus. 3:40 Outro, humming and the spoken line at 3:46.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Retro soul recorded live: warm, a little distorted on the loud notes, plate reverb, the voice exposed.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'I'm tired! Lord, I'm tired! And I'd do it all again' at 2:54.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original is a young woman bound to a love that damages her. This is a wife of fifty years bound to a husband whose mind has gone, which is a harder and more common kind of faithfulness.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Hurt, steady, exhausted, faithful.
